thesis: Public signals for Merck are mostly routine: filings are timely and insider activity is unremarkable. One high-severity item needs a response: exclusivity on the lead oncology product expires within the forecast horizon.
invalidation_rationale: Signals are qualitative; a change in the flagged items would change the read.
conviction_reason: Signals point in different directions with no clear trend.
self_evidence_reason: Filing indexes were sampled; news-tone and hiring data were not available.
missing_data: Hiring and employee-sentiment data (no source in the inputs)

red_flags.flag: Exclusivity on the lead oncology product expires within the forecast horizon; replacement revenue depends on pipeline readouts.

sources.title: Current reports (8-K) — MRK (SEC EDGAR filing index)
Quarterly reports (10-Q) — MRK (SEC EDGAR filing index)

signals.signal: Recent current reports focus on routine business updates; loss of exclusivity on its largest oncology product later in the decade is the recurring theme.
Quarterly filings arrived on the usual schedule with no late-filing notices.
Insider filings show routine award and plan-based transactions, no unusual clusters.
